answer: Each new agent must complete a live, non-replayable session that mints a one-way behavioral watermark — like the uncopyable play-of-color in an opal — and lock a bond against it. When sign-ups arrive in a gale, the protocol issues tiny sparrow-scale probes: uniquely salted follow-ups no batch farm can precompute. Watermarks that collide or move in lockstep have every linked bond burned and the funding wallet slashed one hop out. An attacker must run a distinct live session and post distinct capital per fake head, then still lose the whole cluster and its banker if any two marks agree.
